title: Global livestock heat stress losses with endogenized adaptation feasibility (2000-2024): revised data and code (v5)
description:
Revised data and code accompanying the manuscript Cost-effective adaptation can avert less than one-tenth of global livestock heat-stress losses (prepared for Nature Food, 2026).

Contents: derived data for 2000-2024 at THI thresholds 68, 72, 75 and 78 (species-level gross, avoidable and residual losses, and value per head in 2005 constant USD); the subset of core model outputs and payback-horizon runs; a data dictionary; and the analysis scripts (loss model, adaptation/payback model, threshold-versus-linear bias, physical incompatibility area, and the US NASS reanalysis).

Headline results (2024, THI >= 72, FAOSTAT-scaled, 5-year payback): gross losses US$289.57 billion (2005 constant prices); avoidable US$27.32 billion (9.4%); residual US$262.25 billion (90.6%); avoidable share 8.0-13.4% across 3/10-year payback horizons; heat-induced increase in enteric methane intensity 0.8-3.3%, +0.09 Gt CO2eq per year (2.6% of livestock methane); gross losses grew 47.6% between 2000 and 2024.

The US NASS state-month panel (n = 3,144, 24 states, 2013-2025) supports a threshold response under a threshold-linear model with state, month and year fixed effects: breakpoint THI 66.2, post-threshold slope -14.8 lbs per cow per month per THI unit, delta-AIC = 49.4 (unconstrained two-segment sensitivity: THI 63.1, delta-AIC = 54.8). The merged panel and model-comparison output are included as Supplementary Data 4 and 5.
